chapter: Riddick band and the Fern dances
title: Playing with Tony Fougerat and Jeff Riddick's band
summary: Sal says he met Tony around 1927 and tells stories of Jeff Riddick's band on out-of-town jobs, the drunk amplifier and a wrong-way drive.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition

blocks.x: How long have you been playing with Fuzzer?

Did you play with him when you first met him? Yeah. Definitely. I've been playing with Tony for a half and half years, you know? We got on the house, you know? He called me a long ago. Right here. I was sleeping. And I talked, see? He called me. I want to talk to Sarah, you know? Mm-hmm. She said that he's sleeping. He said, well, it's more important to sleep in the frame. You know, me, you see? Don't call him. Don't call him. Am I right? Sonny wouldn't know from Tony. We had, I played, we played with, you know, we had a pretty nice little band. Not we, Jeff had the band. Jeff Riddick. Hen Ring would play, and Ring was boyfriend, and then had Tony, Fuzzer Law playing, and then had Tony. We used to make all the air basses, Kistler, and what's his name, Lake Charles, you know? All over the place, you know? And had one ball. Why not everybody so loaded up there one night? And from that day, I called him the Drunket in Spanish, you know? Mm-hmm. I said, oh, Boracito. I said, Boracito. I said, I drunk it. I seen him. I said, oh, Boracito, you? Right next to me. Hello, Sal. He said, remember the job I said, I sure do. He said, lost his amplifier. Man, what a night, man. And then, oh, oh, I had to drive back, man. Jeff, he got that loud voice, and I just talked. He says, he wouldn't say he's drunk, of course, the band-aider, you know? He said, I mean, oh, Sal, I'm asleep. He says, would you mind driving back? Vicks, boy, it was raining, see? And they had light on top of the hill up there. I got it up on top, and the lights really had to stop there. I said, Jesus. So, when I go to the start again, I go, I'm going down, man. I'm going down. I look in the back, and everybody's sleeping. I'm enjoying the whole deal. I said, Jesus, God. I'm playing more beer at the country club. See? You know, the bike's kind of funny, there. Because we were riding, see? They called. And we had Joker, Prer. He was playing, Benji, you know? So, man, Joker, Prer and Tony Fuse of the Lord. They were in one car, you know? So, they were driving so slow that Raymond said, more sound, Raymond said. I said, in the back of the car all the time. I said, I don't know what it is. I said, what is it, Raymond? He said, I think the Joker, Prer is breaking them in. They're driving the horse. I said, Joe, he's feeling mad, you see? No, no. He was driving slow, you see? We passed him up again and again. Raymond said, Danny over there. He said, I know what it is. He says, Joe's breaking them in for the, breaking them in for the job, for the drive for the manors, man. So, Tony said, I know where it is. I know where it is. I know where it is. He said, you're torn to your right. We drove up and then, he said, this is the damn place, man. It was a cemetery. It was a cemetery. We finally got to the place and we were playing for another job. We all had these crazy stupid hats, Latin hats with the straws hanging in there. The man said, Jesus Christ. I thought we were hired in Dixieland Band. He said, a bunch of four of us. We were out there with the straws and I, we played another job that day, you know. Bob, when we got inside, the band gave us two-fifths of whiskey. Old Jeff says, Sal, you take that whiskey. He said, no, we'll give us the fuselage. We won't be able to blow a damn note after that. Never stopped playing there, man. At the country club, you know. Another night, the band came in in sections. When we got there, the three-piece band, Raymond Boyk and somebody else, another guy. And we went in another club. We got lost. Some place. I don't know where it was. Oh, man, let's get this kick. He's like history. I thought about it. I got this international magazine the other day. But, Spivax, bitch, what's up there? You know the guy's stupid, Tony, man. It was the job. We couldn't find a place. They told me, it was a base up there. Well, they had about fifty bases up there. I wonder which one it is. He said, I don't know. He said, let's talk about the place, man. We were playing some kind of base here, man. The guy said, which one? I think the Marine base. He said, well, you're only fifteen miles out the way. Fifteen miles. Men's in Florida. So we go again. So I go up in the place. I said, you go over there and see who it is. Jeff said, who's playing in there? So I go up in there and I hear a band. And I come up to get Tony, you know. Man, they got some kind of corny band playing up in there. I wonder who he is. And Tony said, well, Tony got up there. It's going. I said, go here. See what you think about it. He said, he goes up in there. It was Spivax, man. He said, we're not playing there. We finally, finally, we got there. They got three musicians playing there. And the three more came after, about an hour later, you know. We got paid for the same amount of time. We got lost.
